title: Ways to invest in debt
objectives: Compare five routes into debt: FD/small savings, debt funds, target maturity, direct G-secs, direct corporate bonds.
Say what to watch out for on each route.
body_md:
Bank FD/small savings via bank or post office: simple, known return — but premature withdrawal penalties, and interest taxed every year. Debt mutual funds via AMC, distributor or platforms: diversification, liquidity, small amounts, SWP — but NAV can fall and there is no fixed return. Target maturity funds/ETFs via AMC or exchange: near-predictable outcome if held to maturity — but exiting early exposes the investor to rate moves. G-secs and T-bills directly via RBI Retail Direct or brokers: no credit risk, no fund expense — but prices move before maturity and trading is thin in some bonds. Corporate bonds directly via SEBI-registered Online Bond Platform Providers (OBPPs) or a broker, many listed bonds now from ₹10,000 face value: choose specific issuers and maturities — but concentration in one issuer, liquidity, rating and any call option must be checked.

| Route | How | Good for | Watch out for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bank FD / small savings | Bank or post office | Simplicity, known return | Premature withdrawal penalty; interest taxed every year |
| Debt mutual fund | AMC, distributor, platforms | Diversification, liquidity, small amounts, SWP | NAV can fall; no fixed return |
| Target maturity fund / ETF | AMC or stock exchange | Near-predictable outcome if held to maturity | Exiting early exposes the investor to rate moves |
| G-secs and T-bills directly | RBI Retail Direct portal, or brokers | No credit risk, no fund expense | Price moves before maturity; thin trading in some bonds |
| Corporate bonds directly | SEBI-registered Online Bond Platform Providers (OBPPs) or a broker; many listed bonds now available from ₹10,000 face value | Choosing specific issuers and maturities | Concentration in one issuer; liquidity; check rating and any call option |
example: A corporate bond bought directly concentrates risk in one issuer; a debt fund spreads it — that diversification is part of what the fund is for.
say: Direct bonds only through SEBI-registered platforms or brokers.
A debt fund's NAV can fall; there is no fixed return.
never: Direct G-secs never change price before maturity.
Corporate bonds bought directly carry no concentration risk.
